nodes.body: This cache fast path runs whenever a target exists, before `candidate_ports` enforces `--port`. Consequently `--port 9000 --project MyGame` can probe and select a cached port instead of the explicitly requested port, and unrelated cached projects are probed as well. Skip this path when `opts.port` is set and filter cached entries by the target's cached project name/path before probing.

Parsing this as `u16` still accepts `0`, although `--port` is required to be in `1..=65535`. `liminal --port 0 init` can write an invalid preferred port, and `--port 0 health` probes port 0 instead of rejecting the value; add a range validator to the clap argument.

This issue also appears on line 75 of the same file.

With neither `--project` nor `LP_PROJECT`, this `?` returns `None` immediately, so cwd project detection is never used as the default target. Running inside a Unity project while another listener is alive therefore reports ambiguity instead of selecting the cwd project required by SPEC §2; fall back to `detect_project(current_dir())` here.

The preferred config is always read from the current directory, even when `--project`/`LP_PROJECT` resolves to an existing project directory. From outside that project, `--project /path health` will not probe its configured port, so a server running only on that preferred port can be missed unless it is also cached or in the defaults; load the config from the resolved target directory first.

The target-cache fast path currently probes every cached entry matching the mode, then checks the target only after `/health` responds. With multiple projects in `ports.json`, `--project` loses the promised fast path and can spend up to 400 ms per unrelated port; filter cached entries by `project_path` or `project_name` before probing.
